question:
The random variable X has the following probability distribution where a and b are some constants:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline X & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline P(X) & 0.2 & a & a & 0.2 & b \\ \hline \end{array}$$

If the mean $E(X)=3,$ then find values of a and b and hence determine $P(X\ge3)$.
explanation:
**Step 1: Apply the Probability Sum Property**  
The sum of all probabilities in a distribution must equal 1:  
$$0.2 + a + a + 0.2 + b = 1$$  
$$2a + b + 0.4 = 1 \Rightarrow 2a + b = 0.6 \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

**Step 2: Apply the Mean Formula**  
The mean is given by $E(X) = \sum x_i P(X=x_i) = 3$:  
$$1(0.2) + 2(a) + 3(a) + 4(0.2) + 5(b) = 3$$  
$$0.2 + 2a + 3a + 0.8 + 5b = 3$$  
$$5a + 5b + 1.0 = 3 \Rightarrow 5a + 5b = 2$$  
$$a + b = 0.4 \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

**Step 3: Solve the System of Equations**  
Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1:  
$$(2a + b) - (a + b) = 0.6 - 0.4$$  
$$a = 0.2$$  
Substitute $a = 0.2$ in Equation 2:  
$$0.2 + b = 0.4 \Rightarrow b = 0.2$$

**Step 4: Calculate $P(X \ge 3)$**  
$$P(X \ge 3) = P(X=3) + P(X=4) + P(X=5)$$  
$$= a + 0.2 + b = 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.6$$  
Thus, the required probability is $0.6$.
